questions.q: Why do Jarvis and his wife go to Springs?
choices: To spend a day with Margaret's niece Barbara Smith, on a day the Court is not sitting — Jarvis hopes it will do his grieving wife good
To visit the new gold field
questions.explain: The two women talk of home while Jarvis, 'a man of the soil', walks in the garden.

questions.q: Who knocks at the kitchen door while Jarvis reads the newspaper alone?
choices: An old, trembling native parson in black clothes 'green with age' — it is Kumalo
questions.explain: Kumalo sits down on the lowest step 'as though he were ill or starving.'

questions.q: What errand has brought Kumalo to that house?
choices: To inquire about Sibeko's daughter, who had come to work for Smith's married daughter and vanished
To ask for money for the church
questions.explain: The address on his worn paper turns out to be the house where the Jarvises are visiting.

questions.q: What does Kumalo finally tell Jarvis, once Jarvis presses him about 'something between you and me'?
choices: 'It was my son that killed your son'
That he cannot pay a debt
That the girl has run away
questions.explain: Kumalo says it is 'the heaviest thing of all my years' — and of Jarvis's too.

questions.q: How does Jarvis respond after walking out into the garden?
choices: He comes back and says, 'I have heard you. I understand what I did not understand. There is no anger in me.'
He orders Kumalo off the property
questions.explain: He then helps Kumalo do what he came to do — see Smith's daughter about Sibeko's girl.

questions.q: What has become of Sibeko's daughter, according to Smith's daughter?
choices: She 'went to the bad', brewed liquor in her room, was jailed for a month, and was sent away — 'I'm sure I do not know where she is. And I do not care.'
questions.explain: Smith's daughter had promised the father to look after her.

questions.q: How does Jarvis translate Smith's daughter's words into Zulu for Kumalo?
choices: Word for word, including 'And I do not care'
He says only 'She does not know', and does not add that she said 'I do not care'
He softens it into a promise to help
questions.explain: The small mercy is noticed later by Kumalo, who is grateful Jarvis spared him those words.

questions.q: What memory does Jarvis share with Kumalo about Arthur as a boy?
choices: That he was cruel to animals
The small boy who rode past Ndotsheni 'on a red horse with a white face', carrying wooden guns in his belt
That he never left the farm
questions.explain: Kumalo answers, 'There was a brightness in him,' and Jarvis agrees.

questions.q: What does Kumalo say to Jarvis before they part?
choices: 'My heart holds a deep sorrow for you, and for the inkosikazi, and for the young inkosikazi, and for the children.'
questions.explain: Jarvis answers fiercely, 'Yes, yes,' and calls the mistress of the house.

questions.q: What does Jarvis tell his wife afterwards, when she asks why he was so disturbed?
choices: 'Something that came out of the past... You know how it comes, suddenly?'
questions.explain: She is satisfied and says, 'I know.'
